priorities: Determine whether the observed class-conditional effect is specific to the current calibration method
Keep the method comparison controlled on the existing dataset and noise settings
Document differences between methods without expanding the study prematurely
Decide whether the pilot has enough evidence to justify a larger study

circumstances: The researcher follows the Day 25 plan and compares the current calibration method against two existing baselines under the same prevalence-noise settings. One baseline is relatively stable across noise levels, while the second shows a similar low-frequency-class degradation to the current method. This weakens the idea that the observed effect is unique to the current method, but the magnitude and class pattern differ. The researcher checks whether the baseline implementations use compatible calibration definitions and discovers a small but important difference in binning defaults. They standardize the comparison, rerun the affected baseline analysis, and conclude that the broad pattern remains. The researcher records a more cautious question focused on method sensitivity rather than a method-specific failure. A short unrelated programming detour appears late in the day.

activities.title: Run controlled method comparison
activities.summary: The researcher configured two baseline calibration methods, validated the comparison setup, ran the methods under the fixed dataset and prevalence-noise settings, and inspected aggregate and class-conditional results. One baseline showed a similar low-frequency-class degradation.
activities.context: Follow-up to the Day 25 observation that the class-level effect might not be method-specific.

activities.title: Standardize the comparison and reassess the result
activities.summary: The researcher discovered a binning-default difference between baseline B and the main method, standardized the configuration, recomputed the affected baseline, and found that the broad low-frequency-class pattern remained. The method-specific interpretation was weakened.
activities.context: A comparability issue was found before drawing conclusions from the method comparison.

activities.title: Revise the research question
activities.summary: The researcher changed the framing from a method-specific failure toward sensitivity of calibration approaches to prevalence-estimation noise, checked related comparisons in the literature, and fixed a small controlled comparison table while keeping the dataset unchanged.
activities.context: Interpretation changed after comparable baseline behavior was observed.

activities.title: Incidental programming search and documentation
activities.summary: A short search about Python type checking interrupted the final documentation session before the researcher returned to the research question and deferred a larger experiment design.
activities.context: Minor unrelated browsing during the end of the workday.

key_observations: A controlled comparison showed that the low-frequency-class degradation is not unique to the current calibration method.
A binning-default mismatch initially complicated the comparison, but standardizing the metric configuration did not remove the broad pattern.
The evidence therefore supports a more general method-sensitivity question rather than a claim about one method failing.
The researcher narrowed the question without expanding the dataset or noise settings.
The current evidence is still pilot-level and does not establish how widely the pattern generalizes.
priority_alignment: The method-level comparison directly tested the main uncertainty from Day 25.
The researcher corrected a comparability issue before interpreting the baseline result.
The next research question was revised based on evidence rather than convenience.
important_uncertainty: Only a small number of methods have been compared so far.
The observed low-frequency-class sensitivity may depend on the selected dataset.
It remains unclear whether prevalence-estimation noise produces a systematic ranking change between calibration methods.
expected_reflection.possible_next_step: Run one controlled comparison across the existing methods with the standardized metric configuration and summarize method-by-noise interactions before considering another dataset.

primary_action.title: Formalize the method-sensitivity question
primary_action.reason: The pilot has moved from a method-specific anomaly toward a comparative robustness question, but the exact claim and comparison scope still need to be fixed.

secondary_action.title: Keep the comparison matrix small
secondary_action.reason: The current evidence supports a controlled method-by-noise comparison, not a broad benchmark.

things_not_to_do: Do not compare additional methods until the current comparison is summarized consistently.
Do not interpret the low-frequency-class effect as a universal property of calibration.
Do not add another dataset simply to make the pilot look more general.
Do not let unrelated programming cleanup become the next research priority.
